title: Conditional probability from a table ('given that…')
subtitle: Probability and conditional probability · 8 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **8 of the official questions in Probability and conditional probability are this one** — 1 Easy, 4 Medium, 3 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question says 'given that', 'if the person chosen is…', 'of the X, what fraction…', or 'which category is closest to p% of the X'.
- There is a two-way table, and the condition names exactly one row or one column.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Cover the rest of the table with your hand and keep only the row or column the condition names.
- 2) The numerator is the cell in that row or column that also has the target trait.
- For 'closest to p% of the group' questions, take p% of the group total and pick the cell nearest to that number.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Picking out the right row or column is the whole problem, and Desmos can't do that for you.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You divide by the grand total instead of the total of the given group, which gives the 'and' probability.
Or you switch the condition and the target, putting the target's total in the denominator, for example tulips at site A over all site A flowers instead of over all tulips.

sections.heading: You are losing these
